title: Gut-derived IL-17A via STAT3/RORgammat signaling underlies sleep disruption-induced depression: Targeting effects of Schisandrin B therapy.
authors: Xu, Hongdan; Qu, Kankan; Zhang, Zhongqiang; Wang, Yan; Zhao, Hongmei; Fu, Jinlei; Liu, Jialu; Zhang, Yuechun; Xue, Ao; Song, Huizhu; Zhang, Ning
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究睡眠剥夺通过肠道IL-17A/STAT3/RORgammat信号致抑郁及五味子乙素干预，核心为免疫与神经机制，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Circadian rhythm disruption and chronic sleep deprivation are increasingly recognized as key contributors to depression, largely through gut-brain axis dysregulation and neuroinflammatory activation. IL-17A, a pro-inflammatory cytokine primarily derived from intestinal Th17 cells, has emerged as a pivotal mediator linking gut immune imbalance to central nervous system dysfunction. PURPOSE: This study aimed to elucidate the gut-derived IL-17A-STAT3/RORgammat signaling mechanism underlying sleep-deprivation-induced depression and to determine whether Schisandrin B, a lignan from Schisandra chinensis, can alleviate depressive phenotypes by restoring gut-brain axis homeostasis. METHODS: Clinical analyses of plasma cytokines and metabolites were integrated with a mouse model of sleep-deprivation-induced depression. Behavioral tests, resting-state fMRI, gut microbiota 16S rDNA sequencing, Western blotting, ELISA, and network pharmacology with molecular docking were employed to comprehensively investigate neuroimmune, microbial, and neurofunctional alterations. RESULTS: Patients with circadian rhythm disorder-related depression exhibited elevated IL-17A and systemic inflammatory cytokines, accompanied by metabolic dysregulation. Sleep-deprived mice showed depressive-like behaviors, intestinal barrier disruption, Th17/IL-17A pathway activation, and abnormal RS-fMRI activity in mood-regulating brain regions. Schisandrin B treatment markedly reversed these changes-restoring gut microbial balance, enhancing barrier integrity, suppressing IL-17A-driven inflammation, and normalizing neural function. Mechanistically, Schisandrin B inhibited STAT3 phosphorylation and RORgammat expression, while targeting MAPK1 and GSK3beta as key regulatory nodes. CONCLUSION: This study identifies gut-derived IL-17A-STAT3/RORgammat signaling as a mechanistic bridge between sleep deprivation and neuroinflammation, providing direct evidence for the immunological basis of circadian rhythm-related depression. By integrating multi-omics and neuroimaging validation, we demonstrate for the first time that Schisandrin B exerts antidepressant-like effects via coordinated modulation of the gut-brain-immune network. These findings highlight Schisandrin B as a promising natural immunomodulatory candidate for the treatment of mood disorders associated with disrupted circadian rhythms.
abstract_zh: 背景：昼夜节律紊乱和慢性睡眠剥夺日益被认为是抑郁症的关键诱因，主要通过肠-脑轴失调和神经炎症激活发挥作用。IL-17A是一种主要由肠道Th17细胞产生的促炎细胞因子，已成为连接肠道免疫失衡与中枢神经系统功能障碍的关键介质。目的：本研究旨在阐明睡眠剥夺诱导抑郁症中肠道来源的IL-17A-STAT3/RORgammat信号机制，并确定五味子乙素（Schisandrin B，一种来自五味子的木脂素）是否能通过恢复肠-脑轴稳态来缓解抑郁表型。方法：将血浆细胞因子和代谢物的临床分析与睡眠剥夺诱导抑郁症的小鼠模型相结合。采用行为测试、静息态功能磁共振成像（resting-state fMRI）、肠道微生物16S rDNA测序、Western blotting、ELISA以及网络药理学和分子对接，全面研究神经免疫、微生物和神经功能变化。结果：昼夜节律紊乱相关抑郁症患者表现出IL-17A和全身性炎症细胞因子升高，并伴有代谢失调。睡眠剥夺小鼠表现出抑郁样行为、肠道屏障破坏、Th17/IL-17A通路激活，以及情绪调节脑区RS-fMRI活动异常。五味子乙素治疗显著逆转了这些变化——恢复肠道微生物平衡、增强屏障完整性、抑制IL-17A驱动的炎症，并正常化神经功能。机制上，五味子乙素抑制STAT3磷酸化和RORgammat表达，同时靶向MAPK1和GSK3beta作为关键调控节点。结论：本研究将肠道来源的IL-17A-STAT3/RORgammat信号确定为睡眠剥夺与神经炎症之间的机制桥梁，为昼夜节律相关抑郁症的免疫学基础提供了直接证据。通过整合多组学和神经影像学验证，我们首次证明五味子乙素通过协调调节肠-脑-免疫网络发挥抗抑郁样作用。这些发现突显了五味子乙素作为治疗与昼夜节律紊乱相关情绪障碍的有前景的天然免疫调节候选药物。
